aiOverview.content: Robert Mueller, the former FBI director (2001–2013) and special counsel for the Russia investigation, died on March 21, 2026, at the age of 81. In the months leading up to his death, Mueller was a figure in investigations related to Jeffrey Epstein, though his involvement was limited by health issues. Subpoena and Health Issues September 2025: The House Oversight Committee, chaired by Rep. James Comer, withdrew a subpoena for Robert Mueller regarding the investigation into the Justice Department's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein sex trafficking case. Health Condition: The subpoena was withdrawn after it was learned that Mueller had been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in the summer of 2021. Role in Epstein Investigation: The committee sought testimony regarding the 2008 non-prosecution agreement that allowed Epstein to plead guilty to state charges in Florida while Mueller was head of the FBI. Epstein Files Mueller’s name appeared in files related to Jeffrey Epstein. According to a Hindustan Times report on the Epstein files (as of March 2026), communications between associates of Epstein mentioned Mueller in the context of his appointment as special counsel for the Trump-Russia probe. Hindustan Times Hindustan Times Reaction to Death Following the announcement of his death on March 21, 2026, President Donald Trump made hostile remarks regarding Mueller on Truth Social.
